title: Adaptive Report Consolidation — 3 Audience-Driven Reports That Reflect What Was Actually Tested
goal: Replace the current 11-variant flat report catalog with 3 adaptive reports that only show sections relevant to what was actually tested in the run. A LAN scan shows LAN findings. A web scan shows web findings. Compliance annexes are optional add-ons, not separate reports.
generation_reason: The current 11 report variants all use the same report_context() and produce near-identical output regardless of what was tested. A LAN-only scan generates the same sections as a full web+cloud+API scan. The operator specifically requested consolidation to 1-3 reports that adapt to the actual test scope.
scope:
Three deliverables:

(1) CONSOLIDATE REPORT VARIANTS to exactly 3 primary reports:
  - 'summary': Management Summary — 1-2 pages. Risk level, top findings, what was tested, what was not, top-3 remediation actions. No technical detail. For CISO/directeur.
  - 'technical': Technical Report — adaptive. Only sections relevant to what was tested. See filtering rules below.
  - 'compliance': Compliance Annex — optional, on-demand. Maps findings to compliance framework. Operator selects which framework (nis2/dora/soc2/iso27001/pci_dss). Always includes disclaimer.

Retain 'retest' as a fourth variant because it is structurally different (tracks remediation verification over time). Keep 'evidence' as an internal reference. Remove 'assurance' and 'attack_narrative' as primary reports — fold their content into 'technical' as optional subsections.

(2) ADAPTIVE SECTION FILTERING in the Technical Report:
Build a function `report_sections_for_run(run) -> list[str]` that returns which sections to include based on the run profile and findings. Rules:
  - Profile contains 'lan' or 'network' or 'ldap' or 'smb' or 'responder' or 'kerberoast' or 'bloodhound' → include: network_discovery, host_inventory, credential_findings, lateral_movement, ad_findings
  - Profile contains 'web' or 'nuclei' or 'zap' or 'burp' or 'httpx' → include: web_endpoints, injection_findings, auth_findings, header_findings
  - Profile contains 'api' or 'biz-logic' → include: api_endpoints, business_logic_findings
  - Profile contains 'cloud' or 'aws' → include: cloud_inventory, iam_findings, exposure_findings
  - Profile contains 'ldap' or 'identity' or 'bloodhound' → include: ad_findings, identity_findings
  - Profile contains 'intrusive' or 'metasploit' or 'impacket' → include: exploitation_evidence, post_exploitation
  - Always include: scope_summary, findings_summary, remediation_priorities, methodology_used, tools_used
  - NEVER include sections for test types not in the profile (no web_endpoints section in a LAN-only scan)

(3) WHAT WAS TESTED vs WHAT WAS NOT:
In the Technical Report header section, add a 'Test Coverage' block:
  - 'Tested surfaces': derived from tools actually used in the run (tasks list)
  - 'Not in scope for this run': derived from all possible surfaces MINUS what was tested
  - This replaces the current compliance 'not_tested' lists which appear in every compliance variant
  - Example for a LAN scan: 'Tested: Internal network 10.0.20.0/24, 28 hosts, SMB/LDAP/Kerberos services. Not in scope for this run: Web applications, APIs, cloud infrastructure, mobile apps.'

The Management Summary always shows 'Test Coverage' prominently: 'What we tested: ...' and 'What was NOT tested in this engagement: ...'

implementation_notes.report_catalog: In build_report_catalog() (reports.py:4570), return exactly 4 items: summary, technical, compliance (with sub-selector for framework), retest. Remove: soc2, iso27001, pci_dss, nis2, dora, assurance, attack_narrative as top-level catalog items.
implementation_notes.compliance_variant: The 'compliance' report accepts a query parameter ?framework=nis2 (or soc2/iso27001/pci_dss/dora). Default is nis2 for Dutch market. The existing compliance mapping logic (lines 461-899 in reports.py) is preserved but moved behind this single compliance variant.
implementation_notes.adaptive_filtering: Add report_sections_for_run(run) to reports.py. Call it from the technical report builder to decide which sections to render. Use run.profile.name and the tools list from run.tasks to determine coverage.
implementation_notes.test_coverage_block: Add build_test_coverage_block(run, tasks) function that returns dict with 'tested_surfaces' and 'not_tested_surfaces'. Called from both summary and technical reports. Derive from actual tasks in the run, not from the profile description.
implementation_notes.ui_changes: In ui/assets/modules/reports.js, update the report card catalog to show 3 cards: Management Summary, Technical Report, Compliance Annex. The Compliance Annex card has a dropdown for framework selection. Remove the current 9-card grid.
implementation_notes.backwards_compatibility: The API endpoint GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/reports still accepts all old variant names for backwards compatibility — map old names to new: executive→summary, soc2/iso27001/pci_dss/nis2/dora→compliance, assurance→technical, attack_narrative→technical.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Report restructuring and adaptive filtering only. Do not add new finding fields, new API endpoints beyond compliance framework selector, or change the underlying data model.
constraints.preserve_existing_data: All existing generated reports and catalog items remain accessible. Only the presentation layer changes.

success_criteria: Report catalog shows exactly 3-4 cards: Management Summary, Technical Report, Compliance Annex, Retest Report.
A LAN-only run (passive-network-discovery or intrusive-lan-credential-capture profile) generates a Technical Report with ONLY network/host/AD sections — no web, API, or cloud sections.
A web-only run (passive-web-baseline or active-web-safe profile) generates a Technical Report with ONLY web/endpoint sections — no network, LAN, or cloud sections.
Both reports start with a 'Test Coverage' block showing exactly what was tested and what was not in scope.
Management Summary fits on 2 pages and is free of technical jargon.
Old variant names (executive, soc2, nis2, etc.) still work via API for backwards compatibility.
report_sections_for_run(run) function exists and returns correct section list for LAN vs web vs cloud profiles.

acceptance_criteria: LAN run Technical Report has no web sections.
Web run Technical Report has no network/LAN sections.
Test Coverage block visible in both summary and technical reports.
Compliance Annex works with framework selector.

after_completion: Update CURRENT_STATE.md noting 3-report model with adaptive sections.
